title: Minnesota lawyer suspended over fake AI case citations

reading.body:
The article title indicates that a lawyer in Minnesota was suspended in connection with fake case citations attributed to AI use. This places the failure at the point where AI-generated legal research was submitted to a court without adequate verification, a pattern in which a language model asserts fabricated case citations as fact and a human repeats them in official filings.

The full article text was not retrieved, so the specific lawyer, the court involved, the citations at issue, and the precise grounds for suspension are not established from the reporting available. The suspension itself is a disciplinary outcome, not a judicial finding on all underlying facts.

What the title alone confirms is the failure mode: a model producing false legal authorities presented as real ones, and a professional relying on that output without independently checking whether the cited cases exist. A basic verification step, looking up each citation in an authoritative legal database before filing, would have caught the error before it reached the court.
